description: We are a passionate team of students from Cherkasy State Technological University (ChDTU). We are tackling the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge. Our goal is to create an atmospheric, narrative-driven visual novel (sci-fi detective) about forgotten NASA rovers. Our core skills include UI/UX design, narrative storytelling, and data research. Currently, our team is fully formed.
summary: To address the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge, our team developed a concept for an atmospheric, narrative-driven visual novel. Set in 2050, the player acts as a 'Tech-Investigator' tasked with archiving physical files of forgotten NASA rovers like Opportunity. Instead of simply reading dry encyclopedic facts, players must cross-reference incomplete physical case files with an old corporate database to uncover the true fate of these machines.   This project addresses the challenge by transforming raw historical and scientific data into an engaging sci-fi detective experience tailored for school-age space enthusiasts. It is important because it bridges the emotional gap between young audiences and historical space hardware. By gamifying the learning process, we foster empathy and demonstrate that understanding the legacy of past missions is essential for building the future of space exploration.
details:
How it works & What it does: "M.I.A.: Missing in Aerospace" is a conceptual prototype for a 3D interactive sci-fi detective visual novel. Set in the year 2050, the player takes on the role of a corporate Tech-Investigator assigned to digitize and shred physical archives of old NASA missions. The core gameplay loop involves cross-referencing physical evidence (polaroids, engineering notes, physical folders) with a digital corporate database. By piecing together clues, the player uncovers the true fate of missions like the MER-B "Opportunity" rover, shifting their perspective from arrogance to deep respect for these silent pioneers.

Benefits & Intended Impact: The project gamifies historical preservation. Instead of passively reading technical reports or textbooks, school-age space enthusiasts actively investigate mission data. By analyzing clues and connecting different pieces of evidence, the gameplay naturally develops logical thinking and problem-solving skills. Furthermore, the game's framework is highly scalable. While this prototype focuses on Opportunity, future development can easily expand to include other missions (like InSight, Ingenuity, or deep-space probes), creating a growing anthology of space history. The ultimate impact is teaching real NASA science through empathy, demonstrating that we cannot build the future of space exploration without understanding its past.

Tools & Development: Our team developed this prototype over the course of the hackathon. The game’s visual assets, environments, and character concepts were generated using AI image tools to achieve a cohesive Low-poly 3D aesthetic. The UI/UX, game interfaces, and narrative flow were designed and assembled entirely in Figma.

Creativity & Factors Considered: Our creativity lies in transforming dry data into a mystery. We deliberately chose a protagonist who initially views these historic artifacts as "scrap paper." This character arc mirrors how younger audiences might view old technology. By solving the case, the player and the protagonist learn the value of this legacy together. We considered the challenge of making technical data accessible, ensuring that every clue in the game is rooted in real NASA mission facts (e.g., mission durations, the 2015 memory crash, weather conditions).
